title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: The Houthis have moved from Saudi ports to Saudi energy sites: drones were fired at the Ras Tanura refinery and a refinery in Jazan was hit on Thursday, pushing Brent back to about $95. Closer to home, ADNOC L&S confirmed a crew member died after the 17 November attack in Hormuz, and another tanker was hit near Khasab.

gauges.note: Third straight daily rise, up about 5% this week (Reuters via The Irish Times)

stories.headline: Houthis widen attacks from Saudi ports to Ras Tanura and a Jazan refinery
body: After Wednesday's strikes on Jazan and Jeddah ports, Saudi forces said they intercepted four drones fired at Ras Tanura, the 550,000 barrel-a-day refinery that sits beside a major export terminal. Debris fell in the area. On Thursday the coalition said the Houthis attacked a refinery in Jazan.
Riyadh has faced almost daily attacks since early October. Saudi Arabia's economy is now expected to shrink 2.1% this year, the finance minister said.
stories.soWhat: New: Saudi energy sites are now targets, not just ports. Expect Saudi fuel and insurance costs to rise; review Saudi lane prices and keep road capacity from the UAE ready.

stories.headline: ADNOC L&S confirms crew member died after Hormuz attack; another tanker hit near Khasab
body: ADNOC Logistics & Services said the Jordanian crew member missing since the 17 November attack on one of its vessels has been found dead. Eleven crew were injured; nine have left hospital.
UKMTO said an outbound tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile about 33 km east of Khasab, Oman, at 5pm UAE time on Wednesday. All crew are accounted for.
stories.soWhat: New: a UAE company has lost a seafarer, and the strikes are now off Musandam. Sea capacity through the strait will stay scarce; keep pushing east-coast and land routes.

stories.headline: Hormuz tanker traffic edged up in November even as attacks rose
body: Vortexa data show tankers carrying crude, fuels and LNG through the strait stayed above 26 on a seven-day average through 19 November. In October transits were below 25 on at least two-thirds of days.
Shuttle costs and insurance fees are near war-time highs. Vortexa warns that spoofing and dark transits may distort the counts.
stories.soWhat: A small rise in tanker traffic is not a reopening for container ships. Do not plan on Jebel Ali volumes returning soon.

stories.headline: Saudi air cargo volumes down a third; Dubai–Europe rates up 83% on last year
body: WorldACD data for 2–8 November show Saudi Arabia's air volumes fell 33% in the week, and up to 30% over five weeks, since Houthi missile attacks began in early October.
Rates from Middle East & South Asia to Europe were 66% higher than a year ago, with Dubai up 83%. Rates to the US were 79% higher.
stories.soWhat: New angle: Saudi air demand is falling while Dubai outbound air stays costly. Move Saudi-bound express to road and protect air margin on Dubai exports.

stories.headline: White Friday weekend: UAE shoppers keep spending, online tech up 18%
body: UAE orders rose 39% during Singles' Day and gross sales rose 30%, according to Udora and Admitad. NielsenIQ says online sales of tech and durables in the UAE grew 18.3%.
70% of UAE and Saudi shoppers say they would pay more for quality. Trendyol Gulf sold over 3 million products in the first half of its November campaigns.
stories.soWhat: Today is the peak of the sale season, and noon's Yellow Friday and Amazon's White Friday run to Monday 30 November. Volume and returns will stay high into December.

stories.headline: UAE December fuel prices due at month end, with oil now rising again
body: UAE pump prices follow global oil with a one-month lag. Brent averaged $96.91 in the first half of November against $123.57 in the same weeks of October, pointing to a second cut.
But Brent has risen about 5% this week to around $95 after the Saudi refinery attacks.
stories.soWhat: December diesel may ease, but this week's rise could reverse it in January. Keep the fuel surcharge on a monthly review.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: Revised demand surcharge from 16 November; imports to Saudi at SAR 12.4/kg
body: FedEx revised its demand surcharge on international parcel and freight from 16 November. From Saudi Arabia to the GCC it is SAR 2.1 per kg, and SAR 5.8 per kg to the US and Canada.
Imports into Saudi Arabia from the US, Canada and Europe carry SAR 12.4 per kg.
competitors.soWhat: FedEx is pricing war costs in openly. Check our Saudi import surcharge against SAR 12.4/kg and pitch UAE-hub plus road where we come in lower.

competitors.name: DP World
competitors.headline: Over 1 million TEU moved by road and rail; Fujairah terminals brought forward
body: DP World moved over 1 million TEU from east-coast ports to Jebel Ali and inland between March and October, using more than 3,000 trucks, 700 of them its own.
It has brought the Al Rugaylat and Dibba terminals in Fujairah forward to 18–24 months. Al Rugaylat will handle about 2.5 million TEU a year.
competitors.soWhat: DP World is now a large trucking player on our east-coast lanes. Partner on its corridor for freight, and compete with it for domestic distribution. (Story from 11 Nov.)

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Cargo revenue up 52% in the half year on flat volume
body: Emirates SkyCargo carried 1.24 million tonnes from April to September, down 1%, but cargo revenue rose 52% as the war squeezed capacity.
It took five new Boeing 777 freighters and added Almaty and Zhengzhou. On 3 November it also launched a service for AI tech shipments.
competitors.soWhat: The main air seller out of Dubai is earning far more per kilo. Expect firm block space prices; buy early for Q1 and push our own data-centre logistics service. (Story from 5 Nov.)
competitors.imageCredit: Emirates SkyCargo via Air Cargo News

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Data-centre logistics service launched across GCC, Asia and US
body: Aramex Data Center Logistics moves AI racks and networking gear from Taiwan, Southeast Asia, Mexico, the US and Europe by charter and secure road. One crated rack weighs about 1.75 tonnes and can be worth several million dollars.
It follows a record Q3: revenue up 24% to Dh1.98 billion, with gross margin at 21%.
competitors.soWhat: We launched the same week as Emirates SkyCargo's AI service. Move first on named Gulf data-centre projects before air carriers sell direct.

opportunities.title: Peak weekend and returns
opportunities.text: Today is White Friday and noon and Amazon sales run to Monday 30 November. UAE Singles' Day orders were up 39%, so overflow and December returns will be large.

opportunities.title: Saudi inbound via the UAE
opportunities.text: FedEx charges SAR 12.4/kg extra on imports into Saudi from the US and Europe. A UAE hub plus road option can undercut it.

opportunities.title: Road express into Saudi
opportunities.text: Saudi air volumes fell 33% in a week. Shippers need a steady route that avoids Riyadh airport disruption.

opportunities.title: AI data-centre freight
opportunities.text: Racks worth millions move by charter and secure road. Our new service is live; Gulf data-centre builds need it now.

opportunities.title: East-coast corridor
opportunities.text: DP World moves about 3,500 TEU a day by land from the east coast. Our trucks and warehouses can feed and finish those flows.

watchouts.title: Saudi energy sites hit
watchouts.text: Ras Tanura and a Jazan refinery were targeted. Saudi fuel supply and operating costs may rise.

watchouts.title: Attacks off Musandam
watchouts.text: A tanker was hit 33 km east of Khasab and an ADNOC L&S crew member died. Crew and insurers will be more cautious.

watchouts.title: Oil rising again
watchouts.text: Brent is up about 5% this week to near $95. A December fuel cut could reverse in January.

watchouts.title: Air capacity into Saudi
watchouts.text: With Saudi air demand down a third, fixed air commitments into the Kingdom risk running empty.

watchouts.title: Shaky traffic data
watchouts.text: Vortexa warns spoofing and dark transits may distort Hormuz counts. Do not plan on a reopening from one month's data.

moves.title: Staff the White Friday weekend
moves.text: Keep extra riders and sort shifts to Monday 30 November for marketplace sellers, then switch to a December returns offer.

moves.title: Benchmark our Saudi import surcharge
moves.text: Compare our charges on US and Europe imports into Saudi with FedEx's SAR 12.4/kg and pitch UAE hub plus road where we are lower.

moves.title: Shift Saudi-bound air to road
moves.text: Review air allocations into Saudi this week and move flexible express volume to UAE–KSA road.

moves.title: Set the December fuel surcharge
moves.text: Update the fuel surcharge table as soon as UAE December prices are out, and flag that oil rose again this week.

moves.title: Pitch data-centre logistics
moves.text: List Gulf data-centre projects and approach their contractors this month, ahead of Emirates SkyCargo's AI service.

moves.title: Secure east-coast trucking
moves.text: Talk to DP World about feeding its land corridor and lock in trucking capacity from Fujairah and Khor Fakkan.
